samples.summary: List-marker color precedence still treats the legacy `''` as "set", so a cleared marker color no longer inherits the inline's color
samples.evidence: `const colorSource = m?.color ?? firstInline?.color;` — `??` only falls through on null/undefined. After this change `''` means *unset* everywhere else (`resolveStoredColor` maps it to undefined), but here a marker whose color was cleared (`marker.color === ''`) still wins the `??` and short-circuits the inline color, so `resolveStoredColor` returns undefined and the marker paints `theme.defaultColor` instead of the run's color. The new test at test/view/render-list-marker.test.ts (`paints an empty-string marker color with the theme default`, block `{ marker: { color: '' }, inline: { color: '#FF9900' } }`) enshrines this: a bullet on orange text renders near-black. The deleted comment explicitly said the old `??` was safe *because* `StoredColor` had no falsy legal value — that premise is exactly what this change removes, but the operator was not revisited.

samples.summary: `resolveStoredColor` normalizes only the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the PPTX exporter explicitly guards against still bypasses the theme branch
samples.evidence: `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` — the pre-resolver normalization matches only the primitive `''`. The doc comment (and packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:170-172) states the same #728 reset "reaches here both as the bare string and as `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }`". For the object form, slides' `makeColorResolver` → `resolveColor` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102-103) returns `hex = ''`, the trailing `|| undefined` collapses it, and the caller falls back to docs `theme.defaultColor` (near-black) rather than the deck theme's text color — precisely the dark-deck failure the comment says the *before* half exists to prevent. Guard would need `(typeof c === 'object' && c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value === '')` handling too.

samples.summary: PDF export was left out of the new shared color normalizer, so a pasted `rgb(...)` color still exports as black
samples.evidence: `styleColor()` does `defaultColorResolver(hex)` then `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/` and returns `{r:0,g:0,b:0}` on any other shape. The change's own rationale is that HTML paste routinely puts `rgb(255, 0, 0)` into `style.color`/`backgroundColor` (view/clipboard.ts:153, 416) — DOCX and PPTX now convert those via `toRgbHexColor`, but the PDF sink (used by pdf-painter.ts:759 and pdf-table-painter.ts:178, both of which paint `styleColor(...)` unconditionally) silently paints black text and black cell/run backgrounds for the same values. Reusing `toRgbHexColor` in `styleColor` would close the last sink.

samples.summary: `isTransparentAlpha` treats an empty alpha component as fully transparent, dropping a color for a malformed-but-matched `rgba(r,g,b,)`
samples.evidence: The regex `(?:,([^)]*))?` matches `rgba(0, 0, 0, )` with group 4 = `' '`; `isTransparentAlpha` then computes `Number('')` → `0`, which is finite and `<= 0`, so the color is discarded as fully transparent even though the alpha was simply absent/malformed — the opposite of the documented rule ("anything unparseable is treated as opaque"). Same class of gap: 4-digit `#RGBA` and percentage channels (`rgb(100%,0%,0%)`) fall through to `undefined` and drop a visible color.

finding.summary: Table-cell "No fill" reset still cannot clear the stored fill — the #728 reset class the diff fixes for runs is left broken for cells
finding.evidence: The diff fixes run color/highlight resets by passing `undefined` (handled by `removedInlineStyleAttrs` + `tree.removeStyleByPath`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:144/1881). The cell path was not updated: `docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230` calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`; `serializeCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:238) does `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, so the empty string is dropped from the attribute map, and `applyCellStyle` (line 2426) only calls `tree.styleByPath(...)` with no `removeStyleByPath`. Because `styleByPath` merges, the previous `backgroundColor` attribute survives in the CRDT: locally the cache shows `''` (renders as no fill), but the fill reappears for peers and after reload. Same root cause as issue #728, one call site away from the guard the diff added.

verdict.reason: Verified the full live path: DocsTableContextMenu is mounted by docs-view.tsx:582 against a YorkieDocStore (docs-view.tsx:322), its Reset button calls applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" }) (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:229-231), which reaches editor.ts:3648-3671 -> document.ts:861 -> yorkie-doc-store.ts:2406. There, serializeCellStyle drops the empty string (yorkie-doc-store.ts:238 `if (s.backgroundColor)`), and applyCellStyle performs only tree.styleByPath (line 2426) with no removeStyleByPath, while the file's own comments (lines 137-142, 2502-2505) and applyCellSpan (2445-2478) establish that styleByPath merges and removal requires removeStyleByPath. The local cache is set to '' (line 2430) and the renderer treats '' as no fill (table-renderer.ts:175-177), so the clear appears to work locally while the old backgroundColor attribute survives in the CRDT and is read back as truthy by parseCellStyle (line 256) on reparse/reload or by peers. I searched for a counterexample and found none: the only removeStyleByPath sites are 1424 (setBlockType), 1881 (applyStyle/removedInlineStyleAttrs 144-163) and 2477 (applyCellSpan); no '' -> key-removal normalization exists in document.ts:856-863, store.ts:119 or memory.ts:278; markDirty (editor.ts:1415-1420) only invalidates layout, so nothing re-serializes the cell node; no other cell-background reset call site passes undefined; and no test covers clearing a cell fill (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2000-2029). Blocking under the Correctness rubric as a real state-divergence/failed-persist bug (major impact).

finding.summary: `resolveStoredColor` only collapses the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the docstring calls reachable lands on the docs default instead of the theme color
finding.evidence: `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` — the pre-resolver normalization matches only the string `''`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` (a shape the function's own doc comment and the new PPTX test both call reachable) slides' `makeColorResolver` → `resolveColor` (slides/src/model/theme.ts:100-116) returns `''`, which the trailing `|| undefined` turns into `undefined`, so `renderRun`/`renderListMarker` fall back to `theme.defaultColor` (docs near-black) rather than the deck theme's text color. That is exactly the dark-deck failure the comment says the 'before' half exists to prevent, just for the object arm.

verdict.reason: The code matches the finding verbatim. `resolveStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:49) collapses only the bare string `''` before the resolver (`c === ''`), so `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` reaches slides' `makeColorResolver` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52-63), which sends objects to `resolveColor`; that returns `color.value` verbatim (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:100-118), i.e. `''`, and the trailing `|| undefined` turns it into `undefined`. Callers then fall back to the docs `theme.defaultColor` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388-389 and :555) instead of the deck theme's text color — exactly the near-black-on-dark-deck failure the function's own docstring (color.ts:33-38) says the pre-resolver normalization exists to prevent. The shape is treated as reachable by the repo itself (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:170-172; packages/slides/test/export/pptx/text.test.ts:109-124), and no guard anywhere normalizes the object arm before the helper — `resolveColorAtPosition` (color.ts:169,174) and the table renderer (table-renderer.ts:464,573) pass raw `style.color` straight in. Asymmetric/incomplete normalization producing a wrong rendered color is in the correctness lane; nothing here is not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
